description: An attack in which another site makes a logged-in user's browser send a state-changing request that carries the user's cookies.
A random value the server issues and requires in a header or form field, which a foreign page cannot read or add.
Credentials such as cookies that the browser attaches automatically, which is what makes CSRF possible.
A CSRF-token cookie whose value a cooperating client explicitly repeats in the X-XSRF-TOKEN header on unsafe requests.
A Spring Security 7 setting that stores the CSRF token in a script-readable cookie and accepts the plain header value.
Browsers block script from reading cross-origin responses unless the server opts in with CORS headers.
An OPTIONS request the browser sends first to ask which methods and headers a cross-origin call may use, carrying no credentials.
